Setup has written the `dinah` server into `.devin/mcp_config.json` under <BASE>, and Dinah's section into `AGENTS.md` beside it. Both files belong to the Devin CLI, which reads its MCP servers and its rules from the repository. Four things remain, and they are yours to do. Close any Devin session that is open first.

1. Check that this Devin build reads the rules file setup wrote. Run `devin rules paths` in <BASE> and look for `AGENTS.md` in what it prints. Devin's documentation lists `AGENTS.md` first among the rules files it reads, but a build has been seen naming only `.windsurf/rules/*.md` and `.cursor/rules/*.md`, so confirm it against the build you have rather than against the documentation. Where your build does not name `AGENTS.md`, copy the whole marked block, markers included, into a file the build does name, and tell whoever maintains this recipe, because the step is then writing to a file nothing reads.

2. Give the agent's own `dinah` commands the same identity that the MCP server carries. The server entry sets `DINAH_ACTOR` and `DINAH_HARNESS` for the MCP connection alone, and a `dinah` command Devin runs in a shell inherits neither of them. Export them in the environment you start Devin from:

       DINAH_ACTOR=helper
       DINAH_HARNESS=devin

3. Name the vendor and the model each session runs. This recipe names no provider, because Devin brokers models from several vendors and no one vendor is the right default for it, so you supply both yourself as `DINAH_PROVIDER` and `DINAH_MODEL`, set to the vendor and the model of whichever model the session actually runs. Where every session of yours runs one model, run setup again with `--provider <vendor> --model <model>` and setup writes both into the server entry, after which you need neither of them in the shell environment for the MCP connection. Where your sessions differ, let each session declare its own by passing `provider` and `model` on the MCP call. A workbench that gates its columns by tier refuses a claim from a caller that declared neither, as `dinah.undeclared-model`.

4. Register the server again in Devin's web application if you use cloud Devin as well. Cloud Devin and the Devin CLI are separate products, and the cloud one keeps its MCP servers in its own settings, under Customize and then MCPs, with no file to write. Cloud Devin does read `AGENTS.md` from the repository, so the section setup wrote reaches it already. Note that cloud Devin runs on its own machines, where a workbench path under <BASE> does not exist and the `dinah` command may not be installed, so the server entry is worth registering there only where you have put both within its reach.

Start Devin again in <BASE> afterwards, and run `devin mcp list` to confirm the `dinah` server is listed. Where this project also carries Dinah's section from the `codex` recipe, `AGENTS.md` now holds two sections of nearly the same text under different markers. Both are setup's to manage and neither disturbs the other, but you may prefer to take one recipe back with `--remove`, since either section serves any harness that reads the file.
